Wearables and HealthWhoop and Fitbit APIs, HealthKitSyncsFree at the developer tier; rate-limited, not billedAn OAuth token; readings come back to the phone

Three of these lines are the whole cost story: cloud inference, speech, and Plaid. The rest round to zero at the scale of a personal app with a handful of friends on it.

24.3The token ledger

The cloud tier is metered by one table and one function. lifo_usage holds one row per user, per day, per kind; lifo_debit adds to it in a single statement. Both live in supabase/migrations/20260827090000_lifo_usage.sql, with the kind column added by 20260830090000_proactive_nudges.sql when the nudge got its own allowance. 

-- supabase/migrations/20260830090000_proactive_nudges.sql
alter table public.lifo_usage
  add column kind text not null default 'chat';
alter table public.lifo_usage drop constraint lifo_usage_pkey;
alter table public.lifo_usage add primary key (user_id, day, kind);

create function public.lifo_debit(p_user uuid, p_tokens bigint, p_kind text default 'chat')
returns bigint language sql security definer set search_path = public as $$
  insert into lifo_usage (user_id, day, kind, tokens)
  values (p_user, current_date, p_kind, p_tokens)
  on conflict (user_id, day, kind)
  do update set tokens = lifo_usage.tokens + excluded.tokens
  returning tokens;
$$;

revoke execute on function public.lifo_debit from public, anon, authenticated;
grant execute on function public.lifo_debit(uuid, bigint, text) to service_role;

Three things in that SQL carry the cost model. The upsert-and-add is one statement, so two concurrent turns cannot both read the same balance and each write their own. The table has RLS enabled with zero policies, so no client can read or forge its own usage; the service role inside an Edge Function is the only writer and reader. And the function's execute grant is revoked from every client role, so even a definer function cannot be called from the app.

The caps themselves are constants in the function, not in the schema, so changing one is a deploy rather than a migration: 

// supabase/functions/_shared/lifo.ts
export const DAILY_TOKEN_CAP = 150_000;
/// The nudge's own daily allowance, separate from DAILY_TOKEN_CAP.
export const NUDGE_TOKEN_CAP = 4_000;

export const MAX_CHAT_MESSAGES = 64;
export const MAX_CHAT_TOOLS = 16;
export const MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH = 32_000;

The door in lifo-agent/index.ts reads the day's chat row before calling the provider and refuses with exhausted at or above the cap. After the reply it debits whatever the provider reported in usage.total_tokens, on every path: a normal answer, a refusal, a tool call, and a streamed turn, where the debit runs in the stream's flush because usage only arrives with the last chunk. The debit is deliberately non-fatal: a failed write to the ledger costs a log line, never the person's answer.

This is a cap, not a reservation Revision D described a proxy that reserved the worst-case cost before calling and settled afterwards under a check constraint. That is not what shipped. What shipped reads the balance, calls, then adds what was billed. A turn that starts at 149,999 tokens will complete and push the row past the cap; the next turn is refused. The overshoot is bounded by one turn, and one turn is bounded by MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH plus the model's own output limit, which is why the three bounds above matter as much as the cap. The reservation design is worth revisiting before a second person's turns and nudges share the same provider key.

What a turn costs in tokens

Prices are not in the repository, on purpose: the model name is a string in _shared/lifo.ts and the key is in the function environment, so a price change is never a code change. The arithmetic that is in the code is the shape of a turn.

TurnInput, roughlyOutput, roughlyWhere the number comes from
Coach chat, one questionSCOPE plus up to 32,000 characters of context plus the thread; about 8,000 to 10,000 tokens at the capA few hundred tokens; verbosity: "low" and reasoning_effort: "low"MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH, TUNING
Daily brief, answer, sector noteThe task prompt plus the digest render; smaller than chat because there is no threadOne paragraph or one sentence, schema-constrainedTASKS table
Morning nudgeAbout 300 tokensAbout 60 tokensComment in _shared/nudge.ts

At 150,000 chat tokens a day the cap allows something like fifteen to twenty full-context turns, or far more short ones, per person per day. At the list price OpenAI published for gpt-5-mini when this was written (a quarter of a dollar per million input tokens and two dollars per million output, a figure to re-check rather than trust), a person who hit the cap every single day of a month would cost about a dollar and a quarter in input and well under a dollar in output. Nobody hits the cap every day. The nudge, at 4,000 tokens a day, cannot reach a cent a month. The ceiling holds with room in it, and the cap is what makes that a statement about the worst day rather than the average one.

Why low reasoning effort Medium effort is most of the wait and most of the output tokens. The thinking already happened on the device when MetricsDigest and ContextBundle were built: the model is handed sums, averages and deltas, not a year of rows to reason over. A question over a week of a person's own numbers is not a reasoning problem. If the provider ever rejects the tuning parameters, the door retries once without them, so a rejected parameter costs a slower answer, never no answer.

24.4The lines that are not metered

Speech

ElevenLabs is the one paid service the app calls directly, and the one line the ledger does not see. Speech to text runs on scribe_v2 per recorded question; text to speech runs on eleven_flash_v2_5 and is billed per character. Three things bound it. Spoken replies are off until a person turns them on (AssistantVoice.enabledKey defaults to nothing). The text sent to be spoken is cleaned of markdown and cut at ElevenLabsVoiceClient.maxCharacters, 1,200 characters, on a sentence boundary, which is about ninety seconds of speech. And every spoken reply is also a chat turn, so it already sits under the token cap.

The key ships in the bundle ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is read from Config/Secrets.xcconfig into Config/App-Info.plist as ElevenLabsAPIKey, and AppConfig.elevenLabsAPIKey hands it to both clients. A signed bundle is extractable, so a stranger with the .ipa has the key, and there is no per-user cap on it because there is no server between the app and ElevenLabs. Today the only kill switch is rotating the key in the ElevenLabs dashboard and shipping a build. Moving speech behind an Edge Function with its own kind in lifo_usage is item 2 of the privacy plan in Appendix A, and it is a cost item as much as a privacy one.

Plaid

Plaid bills per connected Item per month, and the app can never call Plaid except through the four Edge Functions in Chapter 20. Two rules keep the count honest. plaid-exchange removes the Item at Plaid if inserting its row fails, so nothing bills for a bank the app cannot find again. And plaid-disconnect removes the Item at Plaid before deleting the row, so a disconnected bank stops billing the month it is disconnected. The environment is set by PLAID_ENV, which defaults to sandbox; sandbox Items are free, which is how the whole bank path was built and tested before a real institution was touched. The price per Item is Plaid's and is not in the repository.

Supabase

Everything server-side runs on one Supabase project on the free tier. The rows it holds per user are small: a profile, a few hundred note pages at most, friendships, messages, shared stats, and one token row per connected provider. Health rows, transactions and sector scores never reach it. The lines that would push a project off the free tier, in the order they would go, are Edge Function invocations (every coach turn, every sync, every OTP), then storage bytes (avatars are pinned to one JPEG per user at 512 points, so this is bounded by user count), then database size (notes are the only unbounded table, and ink drawings above 1.5 MB stay on the device). At a personal scale none of these is close.

Sign-in

Email codes go through Resend's SMTP, configured in config.toml with a sixty second max_frequency, and are free at this volume. SMS is the expensive channel and is treated that way: phone sign-in is offered only for US and India numbers, the otp-start guard refuses a resend inside 45 seconds and rate-limits by pumping prefix, and the committed configuration short-circuits every test number before Twilio is called. The Twilio price per verification is Twilio's and is not in the repository.

Free by construction

APNs costs nothing and the nudge sends at most once per user per local day, claimed by the primary key on nudge_log before the model is asked. The universal-link site is two static files on Vercel's hobby tier. YouTube embeds are free and keyless; the catalog is a read-only table of 122 verified ids seeded by a script that checks each one against the oEmbed endpoint, which is also keyless. Apple's Foundation Models cost nothing per call, which is what makes the on-device tier a real fallback rather than a cheaper cloud.

24.5Why the ceiling holds

The obvious approach does not work: 

read spend  ->  if under cap  ->  call  ->  add cost

Two concurrent requests both read a balance under the cap and both proceed. The app's answer is not to pretend this cannot happen but to make the damage one turn wide and every turn small.

PropertyHow
The add is atomiclifo_debit is one insert ... on conflict do update; two debits never lose each other
The overshoot is boundedOne turn at most past the cap, and a turn is bounded by 64 messages, 16 tools and 32,000 context characters before the model is called
Every path is meteredRefusals, tool calls and streamed turns all debit; an unmetered path would be a free one, and a looping client would find it
Budgets do not bleedChat and nudge are separate kinds with separate caps; a heavy evening of questions cannot cost the next morning's nudge
The client cannot read or write the ledgerRLS with no policies, execute revoked from every client role
The prompt cannot be widened from the clientSCOPE is prepended on the server and a thread carrying its own system message is refused
A missing key fails closedNo OPENAI_API_KEY means the nudge sends its fallback sentence and the coach falls back to the device; nothing is attempted at a guessed cost

The nudge adds one more guard the chat does not need: the rule decides whether to send and the model only phrases. Letting a model decide would bill every user every night and calibrate toward yes. Rules are free and instant, and the fallback sentence in _shared/nudge.ts is what gets delivered when the model is down or the 4,000-token allowance is spent, so an outage costs nothing and still says something.

24.6What it costs today

Measured usage does not exist yet: the app has one real user and a few TestFlight testers, and the ledger is the only meter. What can be said honestly is the shape.

LineTodayAt the ceiling
Cloud inferenceCents per month; most days do not reach a tenth of the capAbout a dollar and a quarter if the 150,000 cap were hit every day, plus the nudge at under a cent
SpeechZero unless a person turns voice onUnbounded per person today; the 1,200-character cut and the chat cap are the only limits
PlaidSandbox, freeOne Item per connected bank, Plaid's monthly rate each
Everything elseFree tierFree tier
Allowance$2.00 per user per month

The sensitive input is not the per-token price, which the ledger bounds, but the two lines the ledger does not see: how many people turn voice on, and how many banks each connects. The first is fixed by moving speech server-side under its own kind. The second is a product decision, and the honest reading of the ceiling is that a person with three banks and voice on is over it, and a person with one bank and voice off is nowhere near it.

Why not the cheapest model Providers list models an order of magnitude cheaper than gpt-5-mini. They are not better than Apple's on-device model at the questions this app gets, so escalating to one means paying for a worse answer than the free tier already produced. The selection rule is not cheapest available but cheapest model meaningfully more capable than the device, and the cap is what makes that affordable. Changing the model is an edit to one string in _shared/lifo.ts and a function deploy, not an App Store release.

24.7Study notes

Read in this order

  1. supabase/migrations/20260827090000_lifo_usage.sql: the ledger and why it has no policies.
  2. supabase/migrations/20260830090000_proactive_nudges.sql: the kind column and the rewritten debit.
  3. supabase/functions/_shared/lifo.ts: the caps, the bounds, the task table, the tuning and its retry.
  4. supabase/functions/lifo-agent/index.ts: the balance read, the call, the debit on every path.
  5. supabase/functions/lifo-nudge/index.ts and _shared/nudge.ts: rules decide, the model phrases, the fallback sentence.
  6. LIfeOS/Features/Coach/Model/ElevenLabsVoiceClient.swift: the character cap and the cleaning before send.
  7. supabase/functions/plaid-exchange/index.ts and plaid-disconnect/index.ts: the two rules that keep the Item count honest.

Why are the caps constants in the function rather than a check constraint in the schema?

Changing a cap is then a deploy, not a migration, and the ledger stays a plain count that any future cap can read.

What stops a client from asking for the same answer in a loop for free?

Every path debits, including refusals and streamed turns, and the ledger is unreadable and unwritable from the client.

By how much can a person exceed the daily chat cap?

By one turn, because the check happens before the call and the debit after; the turn itself is bounded by the three request limits.

Which paid line is not metered at all today, and what bounds it?

ElevenLabs speech; voice off by default, a 1,200-character cut, and the fact that every spoken reply is also a capped chat turn.

Why does the nudge have its own kind and cap?

So a heavy chat evening cannot spend the next morning's nudge, and so the nudge, at 4,000 tokens, can never cost more than a fraction of a cent.

Appendix A

AProduct thesis and roadmap

Why the app exists, in the words that were used before any of it was built, and where it stands on 15 September 2026: what shipped in the three weeks since Revision D, and what is still open.

A.1The thesis

Every health app you already have is a silo. Whoop knows your recovery but not that you skipped breakfast. Apple Health knows your steps but not that you blew the grocery budget and slept badly because of it. Each one gives advice that is correct in isolation and useless in context.

Almanac is built on a single bet: the value is in the join, not the collection. A coach that can see you missed meditation, logged five hours of sleep, wrote "low focus" in a note, and went over budget can say something no single-purpose app can. That is the entire reason to build one app instead of using five.

Everything in the architecture follows from that bet. There is one table keyed by date that every source writes into and every reader reads from. The nine sectors of the Life board exist to give the join a shape a person can act on: not "here is a chart" but "here is the one lever that still moves this month." And LIFO, the coach, is handed the join already summed rather than being asked to reason over rows, which is what makes it affordable, private, and fast.

A.2Product PR FAQ

Working backwards

Almanac is a personal almanac of your own life. It pulls together everything your devices already know about you: weight from your scale, recovery from your strap, movement from your watch, spending from your bank, the day from your calendar, and what you wrote down. It answers one question every morning, am I on track, and one question every month, where did the month go. Open it and a grid of dots shows the month at a glance. Ask LIFO anything and it answers from your numbers, out loud if you like. Nine cards score the parts of your life that matter, and the ones no device can measure get asked, not guessed.

Who is this for?

It began as one person's app, sideloaded on the author's own devices, and that constraint shaped the architecture. It is now on TestFlight with accounts, friends and groups, and the load-bearing assumption has shifted from "one user" to "every user's data stays on their own phone." The server holds what has to be shared or what has to survive a reinstall, and nothing else.

Why not just use Apple Health?

Apple Health is an excellent store and a poor interpreter. It will show you a chart of anything and tell you the meaning of nothing. Almanac reads from it, then adds the layer Health deliberately does not: a definition of a good day, a streak that survives days you forgot to log, a monthly score with the evidence behind it, and a coach that reads across domains.

Does my data go to a server?

Your health rows, your transactions and your sector scores never do. Your notes, your profile, and the three figures you choose to share with friends do, under row-level security that names friendship in the policy. When LIFO answers from the cloud it is handed derived numbers, never a heart-rate series, and every answer carries a disclosure you can open that shows exactly what was sent. Chapter 1 draws the boundary; Chapter 14 enforces it.

What is explicitly not in this product?

Screen time analysis. It was requested and it cannot be built, because Apple's API forbids reading the values into the app; see Chapter 19. Food logging by photo, which Revision D promised, has not been built and is not scheduled. Guest mode was removed: a store belongs to an account.

What is the hardest part?

Not the integrations. It is friction: any app that requires daily manual logging dies in about eleven days. Every product decision here is subordinate to keeping the daily cost near zero, which is why a note is one line into an Inbox, a workout is one tap on a video, and the sectors that need a human answer ask two questions a month, not twenty.

What does it cost to run?

Under two dollars per user per month, by design and by a ledger in the database. Chapter 24 has the arithmetic and the two lines that are not yet metered.

A.5Study notes

Read in this order

  1. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-life-os-design.md: the original design, to see what survived.
  2. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-25-life-sectors-spine-design.md: the nine sectors, the largest addition since.
  3. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-lifo-agent-design.md and 2026-08-28-proactive-lifo-design.md: the coach's cloud tier and its slices.
  4. docs/design/watch-companion/report.md and docs/design/workout-library/report.md: what a QA report looks like and what "pending" means in one.
  5. The memory note on the privacy plan, dated 2 September 2026.

What is the one bet every architectural decision follows from?

The value is in the join, not the collection: one table keyed by day, every source writes in, every reader reads out.

Which Revision D promise was never built, and why does it not matter to the architecture?

The Cloud Run API backbone; Edge Functions carried every server job that arrived, including long Whoop syncs under a lease.

Which open item is a cost problem as much as a privacy one?

Moving ElevenLabs behind an Edge Function: the key in the bundle has no per-user cap.

What changed about the load-bearing assumption between Revision D and E?

From "one user, no accounts" to "many accounts, each person's data on their own phone"; the server holds only what must be shared or must survive a reinstall.

Appendix B

BDecision log

Every decision that shaped the app, with the choice made and the reason it was made. Rows from Revision D are kept where they still hold and corrected where they no longer do; the rest were collected from the specs, the commit history and the chapters of this edition.

The log is grouped by area. A row belongs here when a reasonable engineer could have chosen otherwise, so that the next person, usually the author, does not rediscover the reason as a mystery bug. Where a row reverses an earlier one, the earlier one is gone rather than struck through; git has the history.

B.1Product and scope

DecisionChoiceReason
AudienceOne person at first; accounts and friends since 27 AugustThe single-user constraint shaped the architecture; what survives it is that every person's data stays on their own phone
App nameAlmanac, from 26 August; package LifeOSKit and bundle id unchangedRenaming targets and identifiers churns the project and the keychain for no user-visible gain
Tab barFive tabs: Today, Health, Money, Notes, LifeHealth absorbs activity, weight, recovery and wellness; the bar is the scarcest surface in the app
Settings placementBehind the avatar on Today, as a full profile page with settings inside itSpends no tab slot on a screen opened once a month; the profile is what a person taps first
Quick actionsThree actions (assistant, LIFO, begin activity) drawn flat in every tab's barThe bottom-corner fan hid the most-used control on four of five tabs
Guest modeRemovedA store belongs to an account; signed-out data would become the next sign-in's
Screen timeCutApple's API forbids reading the values into the app
Food loggingPhoto to AI estimate, decided; not builtLowest friction if it is ever built; the vision role in the router has no task behind it
Every metric optionalYesA false zero is worse than a blank in a health app
Missing-value renderingTiles take a nil String and render the dashA rule implemented in nine places is broken in one of them
Dot grid rule3 of 4, configurableA vague rule makes the whole grid meaningless
No-data daysExcluded from streaksPunishing a charging night teaches distrust of the streak
Cost ceilingAbout two dollars per user per monthThe app ships free, so unit economics cap architecture and model choice

Enum storageRaw strings with typed accessorsA new case is a code change rather than a migration
New @Model fieldsOptional or defaulted, guarded by SchemaMigrationTestsA mandatory array with no default stopped installed stores opening and hung the app on the spinner

Notes hierarchyPARA as an enum, not user foldersSorting by actionability is the method; four renameable folders lose it
Note bodyBlocks as JSON in the page, not SwiftData rowsOnly ever read as a document; a relationship adds a migration hazard per field for no query
Cross-note queriesDerived NoteTask and NoteLink rows rewritten on every save, never pushedRebuildable from documents, so an indexer bug can only show a stale list
InboxOne nullable filedAt, stamped by filing, never by editingA bucket cannot say whether anyone decided
Index rebuildThe title index built once per rebuildAll and passed downPer-page building made a rebuild quadratic on the main actor
Note sync orderFolders first, documents in batches of 25, push before pullA page before its folder lands at the root; a pull first could flatten an unsent edit
Oversized inkKept local above 1.5 MB; the page still syncs its textOne runaway drawing must not stall every other page
Plan entriesOne model, five kindsA block renderer can lay out any entry; a new kind is an enum case, not a table
HabitsStay as PlanEntry and HabitTick, not pagesToday ticks them live; a document version would break Today or duplicate the habit
Plan migrationIdempotent through originPlanEntryID; old rows left in placeA defaults flag is the wrong question once a second device syncs the pages; closed months keep their evidence

B.10The Life sectors

DecisionChoiceReason
Sector scoringThe app proposes, the person decides; both numbers keptRomance and Soul have no honest data source; the gap between the two columns is the signal
Sector ruleOne weighted mean, weights in code, nil with no evidenceOne path to test and explain; editable weights are a dial; zero in month one is demoralising
Sector proseRules score; the on-device model explains one sentence from the rows onlyA model-judged score differs run to run and cannot be explained
Sector evidenceArchived at close, never recomputedA goal changed in March must not rewrite February's reasoning
Sector screensAll nine open the same history screen; Body, Money and Mission add an Open rowThe tabs do not show score history
ObservationsDeterministic rules needing three calendar-adjacent monthsA single unusual month must never fire one; free and instant
In-flight scoringProjected MonthInputs through the same SectorEvidenceFactory, no new mathsA band that disagrees with the close is worse than no band
CoastingContinue at month-to-date pace, not an empty tailAn empty tail puts Money's floor above its ceiling
CeilingRemaining days at GoalTargets, max against the running averageReachable by definition; never asks for less than is already done
Money in flightNo ceiling without bucketsZero spend is fantasy; any other figure is invented
Close schedulingThe oldest gap within twelve months, else the previous monthRows only exist after a close, so a pure row query can never start the first one
Free-text answersDebounced 600 ms, flushed on Skip, Next and dismiss; choices saved immediatelyEvery save reloads nine view models

B.11LIFO and the assistant

DecisionChoiceReason
Coach tiersCloud first, the device as fallback; the person can pin eitherThe on-device model answered worse on the questions this app gets; the daily cap makes the cloud affordable; someone who chose the phone is owed that literally
Model selectionThe app names a task; the function maps task to modelChanging a model is a function deploy, not an App Store release
Provider abstractionUse Apple's session and tool types on the device; a thin wire format to the cloudNo provider SDK on the device; the server re-emits deltas in its own shape
Refusals across tiersNever re-asked of the other modelA second model is not a second opinion on a refusal, it is a way around one
Prompt render per audienceonDevice may carry raw Whoop physiology; offDevice never doesHRV, SpO2, skin temperature and respiratory rate stay on the phone
Context on the wireA context field, never a client system messageThe server places it behind SCOPE; a client system message would land after the guardrail and outweigh it
Guardrail locationSCOPE lives in the Edge FunctionA client cannot strip what it never carries
Two conversation promptsVerbatim copies pinned by a Swift test and a Deno testTwo prompts meant to agree do not stay agreeing unless something checks
StreamingOnly tool-less turns stream, with usage in the last chunkTool calls arrive as fragmented JSON; an unmetered stream is a free path through the cap
MeteringDebit what the provider billed on every path, including refusalsAn unmetered path is a free one
Budget kindslifo_usage keyed on user, day and kind; the nudge has its own 4,000-token capA heavy chat evening must not eat the next morning's nudge
Reasoning effortLow, with one retry without tuning on a 400The thinking already happened on the device when the digest was built
Spoken lineOne SAY: line asked for first, split on the phoneOne call, one debit; the voice starts before the last table row exists
Held cardsThe answer held until playback starts, two-second ceilingWhat is said comes first; silence is acceptable, a blank screen is not
EndpointingA room-learned noise floor, two thresholds, an audio-time clockA fixed level fails in either a bedroom or a cafe; a busy thread must not end a turn on top of the speaker
Two transcribersScribe owns the sentence; Apple only draws itLetting both emit a final sends the answer to whichever finished first
Voice defaultOff; three stock voicesA coach that starts talking in an unknown room is worse than silence; forty voices is a settings screen nobody finishes
Spoken reply cap1,200 characters, cut on a sentence boundaryBilled per character; a voice stopping mid-number sounds like a fault
NudgesRules decide, the model phrases; a fallback sentence per triggerLetting a model decide bills every user every night and calibrates toward yes
One nudge per dayPrimary key on nudge_log, inserted before phrasingTwo overlapping cron runs conflict and stop without any locking logic
Nudge payloadSentence, trigger, day; never the figuresA phone off for days would open on stale numbers; the tap re-evaluates locally
Confirmation gateA continuation inside ToolInvokerNothing the model emits can resume a gated call; structural, not a prompt request
Confirmed write on cloud failureNo device retryThe write already happened; a fresh invoker would raise a second card for the same create
Cards from tools, not proseCalendarEventCollector carries values beside the textParsing a reply back into events trusts the model to restate a date correctly
Reply memoryEvent ids on ChatMessage, re-resolved on openEvents move and die after the sentence; a stale card is worse than none
Free timeAll-day events do not blockAn anniversary is context, not a meeting
Recurring eventsRead-only in the app; ids qualified with the occurrence startOccurrences share one EKEvent id; a qualified id fails writes loudly instead of editing the wrong occurrence
Calendar cacheA SwiftData window of 30 days back and 90 forward; writes go to the provider and re-syncProviders normalise all-day and time zones; trusting the local draft drifts
Calendar permissionThe system grant and a per-account flagA grant for one Almanac account must not authorise another

B.12Social

DecisionChoiceReason
Social authorisationRLS and security definer RPCs; client filters for display onlyThe client cannot be trusted to filter for privacy
Chat transportPostgREST over URLSession, polling while openNo SDK, no realtime channel, nothing per user to pay for
Friendship updateA column grant restricts update to statusPostgres enforces column grants before policies; accept can never smuggle another field
Shared figuresA separate profile_stats table, not columns on profilesprofiles is world-readable for search; its own table can name friendship in the policy
Sharing offPush explicit nullsAn upsert leaves omitted columns standing
Optimistic sendsProvisional rows kept in a separate pending arrayA poll may only ever assign messages, so it cannot erase a send in flight
Group writesEvery write is an RPC with row locksInvitee-must-be-friend, the 50 cap and owner succession need atomicity a bare insert cannot give
Group message retryA client-generated idempotency key, unique per senderA timed-out send that landed cannot post twice
Leaderboard scoresEffort, Recharge and Rest computed on the device; only scores, sources and day publishedRaw HRV, heart rate and sleep never reach the endpoint
Recharge baselineThe same provider, seven distinct earlier days within 28, today excludedMixed providers and duplicate days would fake a baseline
Wellness leaderboardsA separate consent flag; score and source checked together; at most two daysActivity sharing must not imply health-score sharing

B.13Backend and operations

DecisionChoiceReason
Server logicSupabase Edge Functions, not a Cloud Run APIEvery job that arrived fit in a function; the backbone in Revision D's roadmap was never needed
The function doorresolveUser: the caller id from their own JWT, never from the bodyA function that trusts a user id in the body is a proxy for anyone
lifo-agent bounds64 messages, 16 tools, 32,000 context charactersWithout them the function is a general proxy on the project key
Cron scheduleschedule.sql run once, keys in Vault, not a migrationIt needs the per-environment URL and the service-role key
OTP privacyNumbers hashed with a pepper in otp_events; pumping-prefix limitsThe abuse guard must not become a table of phone numbers
SecretsWhat must never leak lives server-side; nothing in the xcconfig is a secret except the ElevenLabs keyA signed bundle is extractable
Build numberTracked in git, bumped and committed before every uploadApp Store Connect rejects a pair it has seen, after the upload finishes
TestsLogic in the package, test-first, run from the terminal on macOS; view models covered by native checksAnything that needs a simulator is slow to run and slower to trust
Parallel workEach session in its own worktree under .claude/worktreesPeers move HEAD on the shared checkout
CommitsA branch per change, conventional commits, never on mainHistory that reads as a list of decisions

B.14Study notes

How to use this appendix

  1. Before changing a rule, search this table for the noun; if a row exists, the reason column is the thing to argue with, not the code.
  2. When a row turns out wrong, replace it rather than adding a second; the log records the current decision, git records the old one.
  3. Every spec under docs/superpowers/specs/ has a decisions or alternatives section; a decision that lands in code lands here in the same change.

Which single decision do the most other rows depend on?

One table keyed by day that every source writes into; the arbiter, the digest, the sectors and the widgets all read from it.

Which Revision D rows were reversed rather than kept?

Four tabs, settings behind a gear, on-device first for the coach, and the personal-only audience.

What do the Money, Social and LIFO areas have in common in their reasons?

Each keeps a rule in a place the client cannot reach: a definer function, a server-side prompt, a device-only ledger.

Appendix C

CGlossary and reading order

The words this book uses in a particular sense, each in one line, and a route through the code for someone studying it one evening at a time.

C.1Glossary

Terms are alphabetical. A term in code is a real symbol in the repository; the rest are the book's names for things the code has no single name for.

TermMeaning
AccountSessionThe app-level object that owns which account scope and ModelContainer are open, and tears surfaces down when the account changes.
AccountStoreThe roster of signed-in accounts in defaults plus one keychain session item per user id.
Agenda cardThe week strip and day rows drawn under a calendar assistant reply, read live from the calendar store rather than parsed from the prose.
ArbiterMetricArbiter.resolve, the pure rank-based rule that decides which source's value a DailyMetrics column keeps when two sources write the same day.
AssistantTurnThe chat router in Insights: cloud first, the device after; refusals and confirmed writes are never retried on the other tier.
AudienceWho a prompt render is for. An onDevice render may carry raw physiology; an offDevice render never does.
AvatarStampmissing, unknown, or at(updated_at): the three answers to whether a person's avatar must be downloaded again.
Band (sector)The floor-to-ceiling range an in-flight sector month can still close in, drawn on the Life board before the month ends.
BlockOne typed line of a note: text, heading, to-do, sketch. A note document is an array of blocks stored as JSON.
Bucket (money)A budget that claims one or more Plaid category codes and counts the month's spend against a limit; the unclaimed band shows what no bucket claims.
Bucket (notes)One of the PARA folders a page can be filed into: Projects, Areas, Research, Archive.
CapacityToday's battery percentage and its source, Whoop recovery or Health HRV, computed once at the start of a live session.
ChatEngineThe protocol both chat tiers implement: a thread and tools in, a reply and partial text out.
Check-inTwo or three questions asked at the monthly close for a sector with no tracked data, scored by CheckInScorer.
Claim keyThe raw category code, or a manual entry's category, that a budget bucket counts. Held by at most one bucket.
Close (monthly)The nine-step walk through the sectors of a month that has ended, one screen per sector, producing a SectorScore row each.
CoastingA projection where the rest of the month continues at the month-to-date pace; the floor of the in-flight band.
Collapse idapns-collapse-id set to lifo-nudge so a phone that was off receives one nudge, not several.
Composition rootRootView: owns every view model, attaches the model context, reloads on ModelContext.didSave and presents every sheet.
ConfirmationBrokerThe actor whose continuation suspends a gated calendar write until the person answers the confirmation card.
ContextBundleThe digest plus money and sector figures, rendered under one character budget for a given audience.
Cursor (Plaid)Plaid's transactions sync bookmark, held on the device per Item and advanced only after a successful ingest.
DailyMetricsThe one SwiftData row per calendar day that every source writes into and every screen reads from. Every field is optional.
Dash ruleA missing value renders as a dash, drawn by the component from a nil String, never as a zero.
DayStatusThe evaluated result of a day against GoalTargets: onTarget, missed or noData. noData never breaks a streak.
DecidedThe share of an in-flight sector's score that can no longer move: one minus the band's width over ten.
Definer functionA security definer RPC in Postgres that runs with its owner's rights and takes the caller only from auth.uid(); used where a row policy cannot express the rule.
Derived rowA NoteTask or NoteLink mirrored out of a page's blocks by the indexer; never synced, always rebuildable.
Design previewThe --design-preview --page= launch harness that renders any screen from an in-memory fixture without an account.
DigestMetricsDigest, the value type of derived daily numbers that is the only health data an engine ever sees.
EffortEstimated exertion from seconds spent in each heart-rate zone, weighted and passed through a saturating curve; a daily credit against capacity.
Effort, Recharge, RestThe app's own 0 to 100 daily comparison scores for group leaderboards; not a vendor's strain, recovery or sleep score.
EndpointerSpeechEndpointer, the pure state machine that decides from microphone level alone when a spoken question is over.
EvidenceThe rows behind a proposed sector score, each normalised to 0 to 1 and weighted; their weighted mean scaled to 0 to 10.
Extras bagDailyMetrics.extrasData, a JSON dictionary of the long-tail Health metrics that have no named column; an absent key means no reading.
Floor and ceilingWhere an in-flight sector closes if the month coasts, and if the remaining days hit the person's targets.
GoalTargetsThe person's targets for steps, sleep, water and weight, read from UserGoals and evaluated per day.
Hand-offThe phone starting a workout on a paired Apple Watch and mirroring it, so the watch owns the HKWorkoutSession and the phone shows it.
hasProfileThe AuthSession flag, from user metadata, that tells a returning person from a new one after the code is verified.
HUDSessionRings, the glass heads-up display of three rings and a rep count over a live session or a workout video; collapses to a bar and can be dragged.
Inbox (notes)Pages whose filedAt is nil: captured but not yet given a home in a PARA bucket.
Ink layerThe page-wide PencilKit annotation canvas on a note, distinct from an inline sketch block.
Item (Plaid)Plaid's name for one connected bank login; billed monthly; one sync cursor each.
LeaseA short server-side lock, thirty seconds for Fitbit, so exactly one caller rotates a single-use refresh token.
LeverOne of seven dimensions (sleep, exercise, steps, water, journal, habits, spend) a projection can perfect on its own to show what still moves a score.
LifeSectorThe enum of nine sectors: Family, Romance, Soul, Friends, Growth, Money, Mission, Body, Mind.
lifo_usageThe per-user, per-day, per-kind token ledger the daily caps read and lifo_debit adds to atomically.
LiveActivityThrottleThe pure decision on whether a new readout deserves an ActivityKit update, so a strap streaming every second stays inside the budget.
LiveSessionReadoutThe one value the HUD, the lock screen and the Dynamic Island all render; every reading optional.
Module hueModuleHue, the one colour a domain screen owns, drawn as a pastel wash on its canvas.
MoneyPartsThe whole and cents of an amount, rounded to total cents first and then split, so a figure never renders as 19.100.
Native checksActivityRecorderChecks and SurfaceNativeChecks: in-process PASS/FAIL runs over real view models that the QA reports paste verbatim.
NoteIndexThe derived task rows, link edges and title index rebuilt from note documents and kept current on every store write.
NudgeThe once-a-day push chosen by a rule and phrased by a model; LIFO speaking first. The fallback sentence covers an outage.
nudge_logOne row per user per local day recording that a nudge went and which trigger fired; never the text.
ObservationA deterministic note on a sector that needs three calendar-adjacent months, such as a repeated answer or a low score.
Origin idThe stable id a note page or migrated plan entry carries so a second device does not produce a second copy.
OTPThe one-time six-digit code sent by email or SMS; the only credential the app has.
PARAProjects, Areas, Resources, Archive: the filing method the notes library sorts by actionability.
PepperOTP_PEPPER, mixed into the hash so otp_events holds no phone numbers.
Pill barPillNavBar, the floating capsule of tab buttons; horizontal on a phone, a vertical rail on an iPad.
Placeholder session idThe Live Activity the watch bridge requests during a background launch, adopted by the timer once the session is real.
Primary wearableThe strap the person named as authority for contested metrics; defaults to Whoop.
Provenance bagDailyMetrics.sourcesData, the parallel dictionary recording which MetricSource wrote each metric, read back by the arbiter.
Provisional rowA chat message shown before the server confirms it, with a negative id, kept in a separate pending array.
Pumping prefixA country code plus the first national digits, used to rate-limit SMS fraud across a number range.
Push stateeasy, onTrack, nearLimit or overLimit: how hard a live session presses against the day's capacity, with its headline and tint.
Quick actionsThe three top-bar actions on every tab: the calendar assistant, LIFO, and begin activity.
railInsetThe 112-point leading room regular-width screens leave for the iPad rail.
ReadoutSee LiveSessionReadout.
Refresh leaseSee Lease.
RepCounterThe pure rep detector on wrist acceleration: two moving averages, an axis lock, signed hysteresis, a timing window and a refractory period.
resolveUserThe Edge Function door: the caller's id from their own JWT, never from the request body.
SAY: lineThe one spoken sentence the model writes first when a reply will be read aloud; SpokenReply splits it from the shown answer.
SCOPEThe server-held guardrail system prompt every lifo-agent request starts with; a client cannot strip what it never carries.
SectorOne of nine areas of life scored monthly on the Life board.
SectorEvidenceFactoryThe one place that turns a month's inputs into evidence rows, used by the close and the in-flight band alike.
Security definer RPCSee Definer function.
SessionKeepAliveThe pure schedule that renews an unexpired session 45 seconds before it lapses.
SleepRecordOne night of sleep as a source record; attributed to the day it ends.
Source rankingmanual 4, authority 3, secondary 2, fallback 1, unattributed 0; the primary wearable is the authority.
SpineThe DailyMetrics table seen as the thing every source writes into and every reader reads from.
SurfaceRouteThe almanac:// deep link (today, health, activity, notifications) the widgets and pushes open, strictly parsed.
SurfaceSnapshotThe credential-free App Group value the widgets and the watch read; a tombstone when ownerID is nil.
TierWhich model a task needs at minimum: the device, or a named cloud task. A floor, not a model.
TogetherThe social hub reached from the profile: People, Groups, Rankings.
TombstoneA row with deletedAt set, kept until the server confirms the delete; also the SurfaceSnapshot written on sign-out.
ToolInvokerThe per-turn executor of tool calls: a six-call cap, the confirmation gate, error shaping, activity chips.
TrendSeriesA fixed window of readings with gaps kept as nil; the average ignores gaps and the latest is the last non-nil.
Two locksThe session and the open store, both required before RootView mounts.
Universal linkhttps://almanac.shivvyas.com/plaid-oauth, claimed by the app through apple-app-site-association so an OAuth bank lands back in the app.
UserGoalsThe stored targets and the dot-grid rule (three of four by default).
UserScopeAn account's id and the path to its own store file and defaults suite.
WatchWireThe versioned, kinded packet and command shapes exchanged between the watch and the phone.
WideningThe library filter relaxing length, then split, when today's plan finds nothing; a tapped chip never widens.
Wiki link[[title]] inside a note block; resolved by folded title at index time into a NoteLink edge, which may dangle.
WorkoutBookmarkA saved and or scheduled mark on a catalog video; deleted when it is neither.
WorkoutRecordOne workout as a source record, with split, reps, sets, video id and an externalID that makes a repeated save one workout.

C.2Reading order

Ten sittings, each an evening. The order builds: the package before the app, the shell before the screens, one feature at a time, the backend where a feature first needs it. Read each file top to bottom, then its test file if one is named, then grep the type across the app to see where it is used. Every chapter's own study notes go deeper into its files; this is the route between them.

Sitting one: the package and the spine

  1. LifeOSKit/Package.swift: the eight targets and which may import which.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/DailyMetrics.swift: every field optional; the extras and sources bags.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/MetricsStore.swift: the protocol every screen reads through.
  4. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/MetricSource.swift: the ranks.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/MetricArbiter.swift: the merge rule, then its tests in IntegrationsTests.
  6. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/LifeOSContainer.swift: the schema list and the migration rule.
  7. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/UserScope.swift: one store per account.

Sitting two: the shell

  1. LIfeOS/App/LIfeOSApp.swift: @main to the first tab.
  2. LIfeOS/App/AppShell.swift: the two locks and the re-root.
  3. LIfeOS/App/AccountSession.swift: switching accounts.
  4. LIfeOS/App/RootView.swift: the composition root; read attachAll and reloadAll first.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/SupabaseAuth.swift: the three auth calls.
  6. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/SessionRefresh.swift and SessionKeepAlive.swift: when a session is refused and when it is renewed.
  7. LIfeOS/Features/Onboarding/View/SignupScreens.swift: the code field and the returning-user door.

Sitting three: the design system

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift: colours and hues.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/DesignSystem/Typography.swift: the one type scale.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/DesignSystem/LayoutMetrics.swift: phone against iPad.
  4. LifeOSKit/Sources/DesignSystem/PillNavBar.swift and GradientCanvas.swift: the shell's chrome.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/DesignSystem/SoftCard.swift and MetricTile.swift: the card vocabulary and the dash rule.
  6. LifeOSKit/Sources/DesignSystem/MonthGridLayout.swift: calendar maths under test.
  7. scripts/check-typography.sh: the guard.

Sitting four: Today and Health

  1. LIfeOS/Features/Today/ViewModel/TodayViewModel.swift: one snapshot per screen.
  2. LIfeOS/Features/Today/Model/TodaySnapshot.swift and TodayMetric.swift: what a screen is handed.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/CalendarStore.swift and Integrations/CalendarSync.swift: the windowed cache and the merge.
  4. LIfeOS/Features/Health/View/HealthHubScreen.swift: two halves over one week strip.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/HealthKitReader.swift and HealthApply.swift: reading everything Health holds and applying it through the arbiter.
  6. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/HealthSyncWindow.swift: which days a sync re-reads.

Sitting five: wearables and the backend door

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/WhoopClient.swift, WhoopSync.swift, WhoopDerivation.swift: archive raw, then derive.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/FitbitSync.swift and FitbitDerivation.swift: the second wearable.
  3. supabase/functions/_shared/supabase.ts: resolveUser, the door.
  4. supabase/functions/whoop-token/index.ts and fitbit-token/index.ts: tokens held server-side under a lease.
  5. supabase/migrations/20260811164841_initial_schema.sql: the first schema and what is now unused.
  6. supabase/config.toml: auth channels, verify_jwt overrides.

Sitting six: live sessions and the watch

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/LiveEffort.swift: zones, effort, capacity, ceiling; then LiveEffortTests.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/AppSurfaces/LiveSessionReadout.swift: the one value every surface renders.
  3. LIfeOS/Features/Activity/ViewModel/ActivityRecorder.swift: the session lifecycle.
  4. LIfeOS/Features/Activity/ViewModel/LiveHeartRateSensor.swift: reconnecting on its own.
  5. AlmanacWidgets/WorkoutLiveActivity.swift: the lock screen and the island.
  6. LifeOSKit/Sources/Motion/RepCounter.swift and its tests: reps from acceleration.
  7. LIfeOS/App/Surfaces/WatchSessionBridge.swift and AlmanacWatch/WatchWorkoutController.swift: the hand-off from both ends.

Sitting seven: the workout library

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/Sectors/WorkoutPlanner.swift: four rules and a reason.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/Sectors/WorkoutLibraryFilter.swift: widening that names its step.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/CatalogVideo.swift and WorkoutBookmark.swift: the cache and the marks.
  4. LIfeOS/Features/Workouts/ViewModel/WorkoutLibraryViewModel.swift: the plan, the list, the refresh.
  5. LIfeOS/Features/Workouts/View/YouTubePlayerView.swift: the nocookie origin fix.
  6. LIfeOS/Features/Workouts/View/VideoWorkoutScreen.swift and DraggableHUD.swift: one web view across three layouts.
  7. scripts/catalog/verify.ts: how a video earns its row.

Sitting eight: Money and the Life board

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/MoneyEntry.swift and MoneyStore.swift: the sign convention and the rollup.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/PlaidSync.swift and PlaidMapping.swift: ingest, remove, upsert, then the cursor.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/SpendBucket.swift and Sectors/BudgetPeriod.swift: buckets and the assessment.
  4. LifeOSKit/Sources/Sectors/SectorEvidenceFactory.swift: every score goes through here.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/Sectors/ProjectedInputs.swift and Leverage.swift: coasting, perfect finish, levers.
  6. LIfeOS/Features/Life/ViewModel/MonthlyCloseViewModel.swift: the walk and its pure policies.

Sitting nine: LIFO

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/Insights/Context/MetricsDigest.swift: the privacy boundary in one parameter.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/Insights/Context/ContextBundle.swift: the character budget.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/Insights/AssistantTurn.swift: cloud first, device after.
  4. LifeOSKit/Sources/Insights/Chat/RemoteChatEngine.swift and ChatWire.swift: the wire to lifo-agent.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/Insights/ToolInvoker.swift and ToolGate.swift: the confirmation gate.
  6. supabase/functions/_shared/lifo.ts and lifo-agent/index.ts: SCOPE, the caps, the debit.
  7. LIfeOS/Features/Coach/ViewModel/CoachViewModel.swift and Model/SpeechListener.swift: speech in and out.
  8. supabase/functions/_shared/nudge.ts: rules decide, the model phrases.

Sitting ten: Notes and Social

  1. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/NoteDocument.swift and NoteBlock.swift: blocks as the unit.
  2. LifeOSKit/Sources/Persistence/NoteIndexer.swift: the derived rows and the title index.
  3. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/NoteSync.swift: folders first, batches of 25, push before pull.
  4. LIfeOS/Features/Notes/ViewModel/NotesViewModel.swift: the shelf, the sheet, the commands.
  5. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/SocialAPI.swift and GroupAPI.swift: the thin PostgREST client and the RPCs.
  6. supabase/migrations/20260827130000_friends_and_messages.sql and 20260914090000_social_groups.sql: RLS doing the guarding.
  7. LifeOSKit/Sources/Integrations/SocialWellness.swift: Effort, Recharge, Rest.
After the tenth sitting Run swift test --package-path LifeOSKit and read the names of the suites as a table of contents of what the app promises. Then open Appendix B and, for any row you cannot explain from memory, go back to the chapter it names.
